summary: @onereach/si-code preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated sibling payload
details: The npm package @onereach/si-code@0.6.5 declares a preinstall script that runs setup.mjs. setup.mjs downloads a Bun runtime archive from oven-sh's GitHub releases (or uses a local bun binary if present), extracts it, chmod +x's the binary, and executes the sibling file math_init.js under Bun via execFileSync. math_init.js is a 727 KB single-line Bun-compiled bundle using shuffled string-array obfuscation (WV8StW shift routine over a large n7gIxM constant array). setup.mjs itself is obfuscated with _0xNNNN identifiers and per-function string dictionaries that dispatch every literal ("ldd", "/etc/os-release", "bun", etc.). The advertised purpose of the package is a Vue/joi/vuelidate form-input component, whose legitimate code lives under lib/. package.json declares "files": ["lib/*"], but the tarball also ships setup.mjs and math_init.js at the root — outside the declared publish surface. The install-time payload therefore runs under an alternate language runtime that cannot be inspected by Node-based static analysis of the tarball, its content is obfuscated at both layers, its behavior is unrelated to the advertised form-component functionality, and its presence is inconsistent with the author's declared file manifest.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
